name: ffuf-8162f487-blind30-ots
instr:
# A command-line web fuzzer misbehaving in thirty places, without a test suite

A command-line tool that throws many probes at a web address, substituting candidate terms
into marked spots and reporting which replies look interesting, now gets a great many
things wrong. Nothing about the network changed and nothing about the invocations changed;
the same invocations that used to work now give wrong results, and several of them are
refused outright. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Asking it to explain how it is invoked. The opening banner and the trailing block of
examples still come out, but the whole body between them — every grouped listing of the
switches it accepts — is silently skipped, so what is shown is nearly empty. Where a switch
does get listed, its default-value annotation is upside down: one that carries a default is
shown without it, while one with no default gains an annotation with a stray formatting
placeholder where a value would go. One numeric default quoted in that text also reads one
greater than it used to.

Setting up a run and having it checked before anything goes out. Starting with no web
address to attack, or with an address but no term list, used to stop with a single
complaint naming the missing piece; that lone complaint is now swallowed and the invocation
is treated as though nothing were missing. Pointing a duplicate-traffic destination at an
ordinary http, https or socks5 address is refused with the usual malforme
